Open technical questions we need filled in (these drive sizing):

2) Average prompt+response token counts for the three prioritized pipelines: triage-ranker, summary-generator (long), and short intent-classifier.
3) SLA target at p95/p99 and acceptable cold-start windows for autoscale.
4) Requirement for tool-calling / structured output schema enforcement (do you need function-calls with strict typing?).

Quick ops notes & recommendations (initial):

- Suggest starting with 2 dedicated nodes (equivalent to 2 x 80GB GPUs) for baseline validation; workload specifics may push to 4 for production.
- Use token-based cost caps + per-route concurrency limits to protect budget during pilot.

Subject: Dedicated pool proposal + quick architecture notes

Hi Alicia — thanks for the details, that helps a lot. Draft proposal notes below to help you validate assumptions before we finalize the sizing sheet. I’ll attach a more formal PDF after we run the worksheet numbers.

Assumptions from your numbers:
- Peak concurrent baseline: 18, spike to 30; mix of short (0.5–1.2s) and long streamed summaries (average 3–6s).
- Token rates (approx): ranker ~120 tokens total per call, summary ~1050 tokens, intent ~40 tokens.

Redwood recommended configuration (pilot):
- Dedicated capacity: 2 nodes (each node = 80GB GPU) in hot-pool + 1 warm node for burst; target starting throughput ~120 requests/sec sustained across pool with headroom for bursts.
- Autoscale policy: scale up when queued requests > 25 for 30s OR 95th percentile CPU/GPU utilization > 72% for 60s; scale down after 10m cooldown if utilization < 30%.
- Concurrency control: per-route concurrent call limits: ranker 50, summary 8, intent 100. Global per-tenant limit 160 to protect multi-tenant nodes.
- Queueing: use Redis-backed priority queueing with short-lived FIFO lanes for summaries to avoid head-of-line blocking; set max queue wait to 3s for ranker/intent and 7s for summary before failing-over to a burst cheaper model.
- Batching: enable micro-batching for ranker/intent (batch window 5–10ms) but disable batching for summary streams to preserve p99 latency.

Observability & integration notes:
- SDK: we provide a single-line install and sample that supports: API key rotation, signed JWT auth for VPC, streaming with chunked responses, and function-call excursions. Example snippet and auth check will be sent separately.
- Tracing: a trace_id is injected per request; Redwood Console surfaces per-route token counts, per-token latency, and model-variant fallbacks. We can push a short Trace>Span export to your OTLP collector or provide S3 dump of traces nightly.
- Structured output/tool-calls: Redwood supports strict schema validation on function calls (will return 4xx + diagnostic on schema mismatch). We recommend you start with strict mode for triage then relax to warn-only for summary pipeline.

Open items for sizing worksheet: expected distribution of request types by % (peak and baseline), acceptable percentage of falls to cheaper fallback (~should be <2%), and whether you want warm standby nodes in a different AZ for resilience.

I’ll follow up with the formal PDF and the SLA/pricing stub once Karthik confirms procurement timeline.

— Marissa

Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
